recipes.title: Beginner's Sourdough Loaf
recipes.description: Your first real sourdough loaf — simple, forgiving, and incredibly rewarding.
steps: **Mix the dough:** In a large bowl, combine the starter and water. Stir until the starter is dissolved. Add the flour and mix with your hands or a dough whisk until no dry flour remains. Cover and let rest 30 minutes (autolyse).
**Add salt:** Sprinkle the salt over the dough and work it in by squeezing and folding the dough. Add a splash of water if needed to dissolve the salt.

**Stretch and fold:** Over the next 2 hours, perform 4 sets of stretch and folds, spaced 30 minutes apart. To do a set: grab one side of the dough, stretch it up, and fold it over to the other side. Rotate the bowl and repeat 4 times.

**Bulk ferment:** After your last fold, cover the bowl and let the dough rise at room temperature (around 75°F) for 3–4 hours, or until it has grown by about 50% and looks puffy with some bubbles on the surface.

**Shape:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently shape it into a round (boule) by folding the edges toward the center, then flipping it seam-side down and using your hands to create surface tension.
**Cold proof:** Place the shaped dough seam-side up in a floured banneton or a bowl lined with a floured towel. Cover and refrigerate for 12–14 hours (overnight).
**Preheat:** The next day, place a Dutch oven in your oven and preheat to 500°F (260°C) for at least 45 minutes.

**Score and bake:** Turn the cold dough out onto parchment paper. Score the top with a razor blade or sharp knife (a single slash works great). Carefully lower into the hot Dutch oven. Cover with the lid.
**Bake covered:** Bake at 450°F (230°C) with the lid on for 20 minutes. This creates steam for a great crust.
**Bake uncovered:** Remove the lid and bake for another 20–25 minutes until the crust is deep golden brown.
**Cool:** Remove the loaf and let it cool on a wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing. This is critical — the inside is still cooking!
tips: Use the 'poke test' to check if your dough is ready to bake: poke it gently — if it springs back slowly, it's ready.
If your kitchen is cold (below 70°F), bulk ferment will take longer. Be patient and watch the dough, not the clock.
A Dutch oven is the easiest way to get bakery-quality crust at home. Any oven-safe pot with a lid works.

recipes.title: Sourdough Focaccia
recipes.description: Pillowy, olive-oil-soaked focaccia with a crispy bottom. Uses sourdough starter for incredible flavor.
ingredients: 60ml extra-virgin olive oil (plus more for the pan and drizzling)
steps: **Mix:** Combine starter, water, flour, and salt in a large bowl. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons olive oil and incorporate. Cover.
**Stretch and fold:** Perform 3 sets of stretch and folds over 1.5 hours (every 30 minutes).
**Bulk ferment:** Cover and let rise at room temperature for 3–4 hours, or until doubled.
**Oil the pan:** Pour a generous amount of olive oil (about 3 tablespoons) into a half-sheet pan (13x18). Tip the dough into the pan.
**Cold proof (optional):** For deeper flavor, cover the pan and refrigerate overnight (8–12 hours). Otherwise, let it rest at room temperature for 1 hour.

**Dimple and top:** Oil your fingertips and press them into the dough, creating deep dimples all over. Stretch the dough gently to fill the pan. Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with flaky salt and rosemary.
**Bake:** Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C). Bake for 22–28 minutes until golden on top and crispy on the bottom.
**Serve:** Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cutting board. Cut into squares and serve warm.
tips: The more olive oil, the better the crust. Don't be shy!
Overnight cold proof makes a huge flavor difference — plan ahead if you can.
Get creative with toppings: cherry tomatoes, olives, thinly sliced onions, or everything-bagel seasoning.

recipes.title: Sourdough Discard Crackers
recipes.description: Crispy, flavorful crackers that turn your sourdough discard into the perfect snack.
ingredients: Toppings: everything-bagel seasoning, flaky salt, sesame seeds, dried herbs
steps: **Mix:** Combine the discard, flour, olive oil, and salt in a bowl. Stir until a smooth, pliable dough forms. Let rest 30 minutes.
**Roll:** Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Divide dough in half. Roll each piece paper-thin on a sheet of parchment paper. The thinner, the crispier.
**Season:** Brush lightly with olive oil and sprinkle with your choice of toppings. Press toppings gently into the dough.
**Score:** Use a knife or pizza cutter to score the dough into cracker-sized pieces (don't separate).
**Bake:** Bake for 12–18 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through. They're done when golden and crisp.
**Cool and snap:** Let cool completely — they'll crisp up more. Break along the score lines.
tips: These are extremely forgiving — the dough doesn't need to be perfect.
Use discard straight from the fridge; it doesn't need to be active.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
